text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Gunmen attack Iran's cultural centre in the central Pakistani city of Multan, killing seven people, including its Iranian director, and wounding at least one.
- A fire at a huge warehouse of the Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd destroys equipment worth billions of rupees
- Shahbaz Sharif, younger brother of new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif becomes the chief minister of Punjab province.
- Pakistan is planning to send teams of parliamentarians abroad to urge expatriate Pakistanis to deposit foreign exchange in Pakistani banks.
- India is committed to improve relations with Pakistan and hopes for the early resumption of bilateral peace talks, President Shankar Dayal Sharma said.
- Iran has accused the Sunni Moslem militant Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan of attacking the Iranian cultural centre at Multan.
- Executive director of the International Monetary Fund, Abbas Mirakhor, met President Farooq Leghari at his residence.

- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan is putting in place early warning desks for developing procedures to watch financial health of banks and financial institutions and conduct special inspections, whenever considered necessary.
- A delegation of Amalgamated Scottish Oil UK led by its managing director Kevan Fearnley will visit Pakistan next month to discuss with Islamabad, the possibilities of speeding up oil exploration.
- A trade delegation from Taipei will be visiting Pakistan from February 25 to 28.
- The $150 million exchangeable bond issue of the Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd started to snowball in the last 24 hours as the order book touched the $1.08 billion mark.
- Pakistan, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan may ink a tripartite economic cooperation accord at the forthcoming summit of the Organisation of Islamic Countries to support the gas pipeline project.
